text: The Ministry of Communications is a Central ministry of the Government of India responsible for telecommunications and postal services. It was established on 19 July 2016 by bifurcating the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, which itself was split into the Ministry of Communications and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The Ministry comprises two departments: the Department of Telecommunications (DOT) and the Department of Posts (DoP). The Department of Telecommunications, also known as the Door Sanchar Vibhag, handles policy, licensing, and coordination for telegraphs, telephones, wireless, data, facsimile, telematic services, and similar communication forms. It administers laws related to these matters. In 2007, following the increase in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) limit in the telecom sector from 49% to 74%, a new Security wing was created within the DOT (HQ) to address communication network security concerns. The Department of Posts operates one of the world’s oldest and most extensive postal networks. As of 31 March 2017, it had 154,965 post offices—139,067 (89.74%) in rural areas and 15,898 (10.26%) in urban areas—comprising 25,585 departmental post offices and 129,380 ED BPOs. At independence, there were 23,344 post offices, mostly urban; since then, the network has expanded sevenfold, primarily in rural regions. On average, a post office serves an area of 21.56 sq km and a population of 7,753 people, making it the most widely distributed postal system globally. This expansion resulted from the unification of numerous disparate colonial postal systems post-independence. The Department of Posts provides services such as small savings banking, financial services, remittances, insurance, and philately, with about 25,464 full-time and 139,040 part-time post offices. The Director-General (DG) oversees operations, while the Secretary serves as an adviser to the Minister, both roles held by one officer. The DG is assisted by the Postal Services Board, consisting of six members with portfolios in Personnel, Operations, Technology, Postal Life Insurance, Banking, and Planning. Shri Ananta Narayan Nanda is the Secretary (Posts) and Chairman of the Postal Services Board, while Ms. Meera Handa is the Director General (Posts). Shri Vineet Pandey (Additional Charge) serves as Additional Director General (Coordination), Ms. Arundhaty Ghosh as Member (Operations), Shri Biswanath Tripathy as Member (Planning), Shri Pradipta Kumar Bisoi as Member (Personnel), Shri Udai Krishna as Member (Banking), Shri Salim Haque as Member (Technology), and Shri Vineet Pandey as Member (PLI) and Chairman, Investment Board. The national headquarters are located in Delhi at Dak Bhavan, situated at the junction of Parliament Street and Ashoka Road. During 2016–2017, the total revenue from postal services, including remuneration for Savings Bank and Savings Certificate work, was ₹11,511.00 crores, with ₹730.90 crores received from agency charges (recoveries), and total expenditure was ₹24,211.85 crores—up from ₹19,654.67 crores in the previous year—due to increased pay and allowances under the 7th Pay Commission, leave encashment during LTC, material and fuel costs, and service tax revisions. Low revenue is attributed to inadequate investment in infrastructure and technology, though the current top management is investing in modern technology to improve infrastructure, service quality, and to introduce new products to compete. Field services are managed through 22 Postal Circles, generally aligned with states, except in the North Eastern States. Each circle is headed by a Chief Postmaster General and is subdivided into regions, divisions, and further into sub-divisions headed by SSPOs, SPOs, ASPs, and IPSs. Functional units such as Circle Stamp Depots, Postal Stores Depots, and Mail Motor Services also exist within these structures. In addition to the 23 circles, there is a special "Base Circle" to serve the Armed Forces. The Army Postal Service (APS) manages postal needs for soldiers across the country, with DoP personnel commissioned into the army. The Base Circle is led by an Additional Director General, Army Postal Service, holding the rank of Major General. The Department of Posts is governed by the Indian Post Office Act, 2023, which consolidates and amends existing laws on postal services and aims to modernize and expand them, replacing the colonial-era Indian Post Office Act of 1898. In addition to traditional postal services, the department has introduced various new services to keep pace with evolving demands.
